text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The government told Poland's parliamentary committee for integration with the EU that it was impossible to assess the country's integration costs. The government will provide eight million zlotys in funding for the EU Integration Committee (KIE), deputy finance minister Krzysztof Kalicki said.
- The Polish Securities Committee (KPW) has permitted public share trading of the currently state-owned Kruszwica oils and fats maker.

- The Krakow-based Bank Wspolpracy Regionalnej (BWR) bank has taken over the BWR Bank Secesyjny bank and given up its former plans to create a banking holding, as this would entail double taxation, the BWR board president Jan Blajer said.

- Representatives of Polish construction firms operating in Germany have met at the VdPD Polish service sector firms' lobby assembly in Koln, Germany. VdPD is a unique grouping of Polish firms operating abroad and will contribute to Poland's EU integration, Poland's ambassador to Germany Andrzej Byrt said.

- In the first three quarters of 1996 the coal mining sector's net losses exceeded 1.36 billion zlotys and were almost 100 percent higher than in the same period last year, the state coal mining industry restructuring agency said. Coal consumers currently owe the mines three billion zlotys.

- The Sandomierz-based Pilkington Sandoglass floated glass maker will lay off more than 30 percent of its workers to adapt to actual production needs, the Pilkington Sandoglass director general Jonas Borup said. It now employs 1,250 workers.

- A share issue prospectus of the Kwiatkowski National Investment Fund (NFI) will be presented to the Securities Commission (KPW) by the weekend, the treasury vice-minister responsible for privatisation Wieslaw Kaczmarek said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland's industrial output in October was 7.5 percent higher than in September and exceeded last year's results in the same period by 13.9 percent, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- A new gas bottle production plant has been set up in Mielec, southeastern Poland. The plant will produce 11 kg bottles to contain liquified petroleum gas (LPG).
- Norway's Statoil has opened a petrol station in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, southern Poland. Currently, Statoil operates 37 stations around Poland.
- Poland's flagship carrier LOT Airlines have acquired a high-tech Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) telephone exchange from Ericsson.
- Poland's treasury ministry plans to privatise the Lezajsk breweries by the start of December, the vice-minister responsible for privatisation Wieslaw Kaczmarek said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Sweden's IKEA furniture chain will open an outlet in Wroclaw, its fifth in Poland. The shop cost $15 million to build.
- The Dutch Makro Cash and Carry wholesale chain has invested $50 million in its tenth shopping centre, located in Szczecin, northwestern Poland.
ZYCIE

- Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), Poland's telecom monopolist, and the U.S. Microsoft software firm will cooperate in Poland's internet services development. TPSA will distribute Microsoft standard browsers to customers free of charge.
- The listed Optimus computer maker has invested 10 billion zlotys in Poland's internet service market development.
PARKIET
- The listed Swarzedz furniture maker earned a net profit in October for the first time in several months as the result of the company's restructuring, its management said.
- The Kompap paper maker's share price has risen by 12.4 percent since its recent listing, reaching 28.1 zlotys, which was a moderately good result, Kompap president Jerzy Wolkowski said.
- IB Austria Securities recommended buying the Drosed poultry processor's shares and praised its aggressive expansion strategy in a report dated October 21.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
